speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
title: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: Elder Paul H. Sinclair spoke about “Quick to Help, Slow to Judge”.

quotes.text: That Sabbath morning, my young friend James was wearing a new suit. As the program began, James was examining some of the more interesting aspects of his new suit. What most captured his attention were two features of his jacket. On his jacket sleeves there were buttons but no holes. And on the left lapel of his jacket there was a buttonhole but no buttons. Neither the buttons nor the buttonhole seemed to be serving any real purpose.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Well, James cleverly devised a purpose for both. I anxiously watched as James delightedly buttoned his right sleeve to his left jacket lapel. Being pleased with himself quickly gave way to being panicked, because once James had buttoned his arm to his chest, even with the flexibility of a Primary child, he could not get himself loose. James had unintentionally, but quite successfully, created a one-arm straitjacket.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Just then I noticed the little girl sitting next to James. She had also witnessed James’s predicament and his growing concern. But instead of being aggravated, she wanted to help. Quickly discerning what action was needed, she reached up with her tiny, nonjudgmental fingers and popped the button out of the buttonhole. James was rescued, and the Primary program was saved!
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: The Savior taught this loving principle of discipleship from the very beginning of His mortal ministry. In the Gospel of John, He ministers to a Samaritan woman. We do not know her name. We have come to know her as “the woman at the well.” Her interaction with the Lord Jesus Christ teaches many lessons. One critical lesson is the example of the Savior being quick to offer grace and transformative help.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: As the conversation opened, Jesus was weary and unexpectedly asked the woman for a drink. We can only imagine how many days this woman had been coming to this well at this hour, alone—until this day. To her, it was an ordinary day—until Jesus showed up. In her ordinary days, she may have endured many judging eyes but few helping hands—until this day.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: What did Christ focus on instead? Help. The offer of “living water.” The Great Redeemer of all knew absolutely everything about this unnamed woman, and He came to her to be a living witness of living water. He offered her grace and transformative help.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: He spoke to the woman with dignity, not shame. He earnestly listened to her questions and responded with teaching, not ridicule. He did not hold her hostage to her history. He trusted her with truth. Jesus Christ reminds us that to help people transform their lives, we must look not only to their past—we must look to their possible. She walked to the well that day as a pariah. She walked away from the well with a purpose. That is precisely what “quick to help and slow to judge” looks like.
quotes.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference
